shouldFix.title: archiveProfile asserts that CI-1 pins archiveProfileId; CI-1 pins no such thing and no CI rule mentions the token
detail: archiveProfile.emittedAs states: 'OC-2 and conformanceReport.subject.archiveProfileId MUST equal opensip-archive-profile.1. CI-1 pins that token.'

CI-1 reads in full: 'Every input is named and digest-pinned: source tree, tool closure, adapter version, platform target, exception-approval records if any.' It names five input classes and archiveProfileId is none of them. I searched every hermeticCI rule for the token and none contains it.

The mismatch is also categorical, not just a missing list item: CI-1 governs the pinning of adapter-run INPUTS, whereas archiveProfileId is an emitted output token appearing at OC-2 and at conformanceReport.subject. Adding it to CI-1 as written would be a category error; it needs its own clause or a report-side rule.

honestyRepairsFromV3[1] repeats the claim to the coordinator: 'archiveProfileId emitted and CI-pinned.' Emitted is true - I confirmed the token at OC-2 and in conformanceReport.subject. CI-pinned is not.

The v4 closed roster does not include /hermeticCI, so under the artifact's own succession discipline CI-1 could not have been amended this generation. That explains the gap but leaves the assertion standing.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: The profile's whole value is that a single token expands to one byte-level encoding, and emittedAs is where the artifact says that token is held stable. A pin that does not exist means nothing in hermeticCI prevents two runs from claiming different profile ids, and a reader auditing the claim finds CI-1 saying something else entirely. This is the artifact asserting its own enforcement.
shouldFix.whyNotABlocker: Nothing unsafe is authorized and the token is genuinely emitted at both required sites; the defect is a false cross-reference plus a missing rule, both cheap to close.
shouldFix.remedy: Add archiveProfileId to a CI rule - either extend CI-1 to cover emitted profile tokens or add a CI-5 requiring the report's archiveProfileId to equal the profile id - put /hermeticCI on the roster, and correct honestyRepairsFromV3[1] if the rule does not land.

shouldFix.title: archiveProfile calls itself a closed profile, but symlink linkname and the end-of-archive trailer are unspecified, so archiveDigest is not determined for trees containing symlinks and is not determined at all for the archive tail
detail: This is a large advance on v3, which named no parameters at all. v4 closes the classic reproducibility offenders: mtime 0, uid 0, gid 0, uname and gname empty, mode from TreeCommitment.mode, magic ustar\0, version 00, prefix empty with over-long paths refused rather than split, member order by Unicode code-point over the NFC path string, and compression none with gzip/xz/zip explicitly inadmissible. I record that as real work.

It is nonetheless not closed at the byte level. I searched the whole archiveProfile block for each remaining ustar determinant and every one is absent: linkname, target, trailer, end-of-archive, padding, block, devmajor, devminor, checksum, size.

SYMLINKS. metadata.typeflag admits 'file/dir/symlink only', so symlink members are in scope. A ustar symlink member carries its target in the 100-byte linkname field. The profile never says what goes there. The source datum exists and the artifact could have named it: schemas.v11's treeCommitmentShape defines entries as { path, type: 'file'|'dir'|'symlink', mode, length (files only), sha256 (files only), TARGET: relative path (symlinks only) }. Without 'linkname = TreeCommitment.target', a symlink member's bytes are undetermined and archiveDigest is undetermined for any tree containing one.

TRAILER. A ustar stream ends with zero blocks, and implementations differ on how many: POSIX requires at least two 512-byte blocks, while common writers pad the whole archive to a fixed blocking factor - GNU tar's default is 10240 bytes. The profile states no trailer or blocking rule, so two adapters that agree on every named field still produce archives of different total length and therefore different archiveDigest.

SMALLER RESIDUE. devmajor/devminor encoding, the size field for dir and symlink members, the header checksum's terminator convention, and octal-versus-base-256 numeric encoding are all unspecified and all affect bytes.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: archiveProfile.standing claims 'Closed profile' and CI-3 rides byte-identity on exactly that claim - 'Byte-identical archives ride archiveProfile in this artifact, not canonical JSON / ID-DEP-1.' The ride is the artifact's answer to Codex CPCV3-B2 and to my V3-S2. If the profile does not determine the bytes for symlink members or the tail, CI-3's 'same archiveDigest' is not achievable from the contract for a realistic tree, and archiveProfileId names a token that expands to more than one byte string.
shouldFix.whyNotABlocker: The detachment from canonical JSON and ID-DEP-1 is correct and complete, the token is emitted and reported, and the named parameters already remove the dominant sources of nondeterminism. What remains is a bounded completion of a profile that now has the right shape, not a design error.
shouldFix.remedy: State linkname = TreeCommitment.target for symlink members; state the trailer exactly (for example two 512-byte zero blocks and no further padding, so total length is a deterministic function of the member set); and fix devmajor/devminor, the dir/symlink size field, the checksum terminator, and numeric-field encoding to one named convention. None of this chooses a tar implementation, which doesNotChoose correctly reserves.

shouldFix.title: appliesFindingsOf records the Codex v3 verdict as carrying no advisories when it carries two, and notFoldedThisSuccessor is emptied, so CPCV3-A1 and CPCV3-A2 disappear from the record while both remain substantively live
detail: I enumerated the Codex v3 verdict at the pinned digest df42f687...: verdict REJECT, blockers CPCV3-B1 and CPCV3-B2, shouldFix CPCV3-S1 and CPCV3-S2, and advisories CPCV3-A1 and CPCV3-A2.
v4's codexV3 record reproduces the blockers and shouldFix correctly and then states 'advisories': []. That is false about the source file.

notFoldedThisSuccessor went from one entry in v3 to an empty array in v4, so the two advisories are not recorded as carried either. The idCollisionNote likewise enumerates only 'CPCV3-B1/B2/S1/S2'. Between the three fields there is no trace of them, and honestyRepairsFromV3's six entries cover B1, B2 with my S2, S1, S2, my S1 and my ADV-1 - neither Codex advisory.

Both are still live, which I checked rather than assumed. CPCV3-A1 targets a stale reviewGuidance instruction; that instruction is still present verbatim at reviewGuidance.forTheIndependentReviewer[8], reading 'This artifact is a first candidate. Predecessor-finding accounting is N/A' - untrue of a v4 with a pinned v3 predecessor, an appliesFindingsOf block and six claimed repairs. CPCV3-A2 asks whether the report's opaque runId is inside or outside CI-3's reproducible tuple; conformanceReport.shape.inputPins still reads 'runId: opaque' and CI-3 still does not mention runId, so the tension Codex named is unchanged.

The contrast is instructive: my own advisory is handled correctly - recorded as CLAUDE-V3-ADV-1 in claude2v3, disclosed in the idCollisionNote, and folded at honestyRepairsFromV3[5]. The Codex pair got neither treatment.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: Carrying an advisory unfolded is legitimate; recording a REJECT verdict as containing no advisories is not, because appliesFindingsOf is the record a later reviewer walks to check that nothing was dropped. Here the mechanism that exists for exactly this - notFoldedThisSuccessor - was emptied in the same revision that needed it.
shouldFix.whyNotABlocker: Both are advisory-grade in the source verdict, neither bears on the packaging obligations, and CPCV3-A1's target is a stale instruction that misleads nobody who reads the surrounding block.
shouldFix.remedy: Set codexV3.advisories to ['CODEX-V3-A1','CODEX-V3-A2'], list them in notFoldedThisSuccessor if they are carried, name them in the idCollisionNote, and either historicalize reviewGuidance[8] and resolve runId's status in CI-3, or state plainly that both remain owed on a successor.

advisories.title: reviewGuidance is append-only by roster, so a stale instruction now sits among 27 items that contradict it
advisories.detail: The v4 roster names '/reviewGuidance/forTheIndependentReviewer (append)', and eight items were appended, taking the list from 19 to 27. Item [8] still instructs the reviewer that 'This artifact is a first candidate. Predecessor-finding accounting is N/A', while items [17] and the new tail direct the reviewer to audit the v3-to-v4 delta and the folded findings. A reviewer following the list top-down is told first that succession accounting does not apply and later that it is the main thing to attack. Append-only is a sound default for a closed roster, but it cannot correct a carried instruction that has become false; this successor needed an explicit edit slot for that item. Reported separately from V4-S3 because that finding is about the accounting record and this is about the instruction the reviewer actually reads.
advisories.notBlocking: The later items are unambiguous and I followed them; no measurement depends on item [8].
